transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net TV technical operations, my name is Richard. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Richard, my name is Xavier Dupont. We have an S-Net TV 4K box connected to a new LG OLED television, and whenever we watch 4K HDR sports or blockbuster movies, the picture displays terrible posterization and color banding with harsh jagged rings around dark shadows and skies instead of smooth gradations!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon. If I understand correctly, your TV 4K box is experiencing severe color banding and posterization artifacts during 4K HDR playback on your LG OLED display, creating visible rings around dark scenes and skies. Let me query your set-top box HDMI handshake registers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our TV box serial is SN-TV-551029, account reference SN-881920, registered at 12 Trinity Square, Cambridge, CB2 1TT, security PIN 3391.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that brings up the Cambridge TV equipment record.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why would a 4K box produce color banding on an OLED screen?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could I place you on hold for two minutes while I query your set-top box HDMI EDID video payload and chroma subsampling telemetry?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding. Looking at the HDMI EDID link diagnostics, the set-top box is negotiating an 8-bit YCbCr 4:2:0 color space rather than a 10-bit HDR10 color format.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why is it negotiating 8-bit color instead of 10-bit HDR?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The HDMI cable between your box and the television is failing high-speed TMDS clock validation, causing the hardware to throttle down from 18 Gbps to 10.2 Gbps.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we change the HDMI settings on the TV box to force 10-bit color?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Forcing 10-bit color over an insufficient HDMI cable causes complete screen blackouts; however, we can switch the box to YCbCr 4:2:2 10-bit limited range as a temporary stabilizing profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How do we adjust that setting?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Richard? Are you still there? The phone line went completely silent for forty seconds!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I was pushing the HDMI profile modification payload to your set-top box.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will changing the profile eliminate the jagged rings?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously 4K HDR video requires high-bandwidth certified Ultra High Speed HDMI cabling to transmit uncompressed 10-bit color matrices.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, I understand high bandwidth is necessary for 10-bit HDR.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am sending a certified Ultra High Speed 48 Gbps HDMI 2.1 braided cable from our equipment logistics center.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will permanently solve the bandwidth bottleneck.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am a retired film editor and tonight my grandchildren are coming over to our house to watch the 4K HDR premiere of an animated movie that I personally edited the color grading for before I retired! This family movie night is the first time my young grandchildren will see their grandfather's cinematic work on television! If the screen displays ugly jagged pixel rings and ruinous posterization, my grandchildren will be disappointed and my heart will break! I am so distressed!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how deeply important this family movie night is for you, especially with your grandchildren visiting to watch your own color grading work on an animated classic. Having your cinematic work marred by HDMI bandwidth compression is heartbreaking, and I will make sure we optimize your TV box settings right now so tonight's film displays beautiful, smooth color gradations, and dispatch a certified HDMI 2.1 cable for tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Richard, let's optimize the settings right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On your TV box remote, open Settings, go to Picture & Sound, select HDMI Resolution, and choose '4K 10-Bit YCbCr 4:2:2'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Selecting '4K 10-Bit YCbCr 4:2:2'... Pressing confirm... Screen went black for two seconds and returned.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now play a scene from your animated movie that previously showed severe banding.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Loading movie scene with the sunset and dark shadows... Richard! The sunset is rendering smoothly with 90% of the banding completely eliminated! The colors look vibrant and natural!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That interim profile stabilizes the 10-bit color depth within your existing cable's bandwidth limit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My grandchildren will be able to enjoy the film in gorgeous quality tonight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once our certified Ultra High Speed HDMI 2.1 cable arrives tomorrow, you can enable full uncompressed 12-bit RGB 4:4:4 color.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will achieve absolute reference studio perfection.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your HDMI 2.1 cable dispatch consignment reference is CAB-HDMI-88192-C.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: CAB-HDMI-88192-C, noted down.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello? Richard? Did the line drop again? Why does your headset keep cutting out?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I was waiving the standard thirty-pound cable dispatch charge on your account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you for waiving the charge, Richard.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The new cable will arrive via Royal Mail Tracked 24 tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Tomorrow morning, excellent.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have included step-by-step OLED calibration guidance inside the package.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will be very useful for my TV settings.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have a magical family movie night with your grandchildren tonight.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You have brought immense happiness to our home today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just making sure our premises records match perfectly: that was 12 Trinity Square, wasn't it?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 12 Trinity Square, Cambridge.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, hardware serial confirmed on the logistics order.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Richard for your expert help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has been my pleasure assisting. Enjoy the premiere tonight.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Richard.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other TV issue today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net TV technical operations. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
